title: Technical Reference
summary: A compact, implementation-aligned specification of Osiris tokens, grammar, declarations, expressions, values, runtime names, modules, backends, and command-line surface.

sections.title: Source Text, Tokens, and Keywords
sections.summary: Osiris source is UTF-8 text. The lexer tracks one-based line and Unicode-column positions and rejects an unexpected character at its source location.
paragraphs: Unicode whitespace separates tokens. `#` and `//` introduce line comments; there is no block-comment token. A semicolon is an explicit statement separator, while newlines are otherwise whitespace.
Identifiers begin with `_` or a Unicode letter and continue with `_`, Unicode letters, or Unicode digits. Names are case-sensitive.

syntax.label: LEXICAL GRAMMAR

tables.title: Token classes
rows: `const let var emit macro func return try catch while for in break continue package export enum import match switch as true false null`
These always lex as keyword tokens.
These lex as identifiers and acquire special meaning only inside patterns or match arms.
`:` currently introduces an enum backing type; typed `let` deliberately has no colon.
`?` is postfix propagation except immediately after `let`, where it forms `let?`.

tables.title: String escapes
rows: the character itself; the backslash is discarded

sections.title: Declarations and Bindings
sections.summary: Declarations introduce immutable lexical names, explicit mutable locals, module metadata, imports/exports, functions, macros, and nominal enums.
paragraphs: `let` binds the value of its initializer. `let?` first unwraps a `Result` or `Option`. `var` installs a mutable local cell, and `name = expression` replaces it only after the right-hand side succeeds. A typed binding checks a canonical runtime kind; it is not an implicit conversion.

Functions close over lexical scope and may annotate parameters and results without a colon. The checker declares signatures before checking bodies, so recursive groups do not require execution. Macros are compile-time AST substitutions with named parameters. Export declarations name the public bindings of a file module.

The declaration forms are `const name = constExpression`, `let name = expression`, and `var name = expression`; assignment is `name = expression`. `constExpression` is limited to literals, earlier constants, pure unary/binary operations, lists, and tuples.

syntax.label: DECLARATION GRAMMAR
syntax.code:
packageDecl := "package" identifier [ number | string ]
exportDecl  := "export" identifier { "," identifier }
importDecl  := "import" string "as" identifier
letDecl     := "let" [ "?" ] identifier [ type ] "=" expression
funcDecl    := "func" identifier "(" parameters ")" [ type ]
               ( "=>" expression | block )
parameter   := identifier [ type ]
parameters  := [ parameter { "," parameter } ]
type        := canonicalType | "func" "(" [ type { "," type } ] ")" type
macroDecl   := "macro" identifier "(" [ names ] ")" "=>" expression
enumDecl    := "enum" identifier [ ":" enumBacking ] "{" enumCases "}"
names       := identifier { "," identifier }

syntax.label: ENUM CASE GRAMMAR
syntax.code:
enumCase         := identifier [ "(" [ names ] ")" ]
backedEnumCase   := identifier "=" literal
backingType      := string | int | integer | byte | i8 | i16 | i32 | i64 | u8 | u16 | u32 | u64

tables.title: Canonical binding annotations
rows: Requires `number`; an unsuffixed non-negative integer literal may be fitted by the declaration.
Requires the exact unpacked width; an in-range unsuffixed non-negative integer literal may be fitted.
Requires the exact width; an in-range unsuffixed non-negative integer literal may be fitted.
Requires the exact explicit float width.
`string bool null list tensor enum function duration datetime location`
Requires the exact runtime kind; payload/result type parameters are reserved for generic types.
`decimal fixed interval modint complex bigint bigfloat quantity dual`
Requires the exact runtime family and preserves its width, unit, modulus, interval, or derivative metadata.
Requires the exact invariant parameter and result signature. The broad `function` kind accepts any callable.

sections.title: Initialization and Conversion
sections.summary: Every `let` or `var` initializer is evaluated before the binding is installed. A `var` assignment evaluates and validates its right-hand side before committing the replacement.
paragraphs: `let size u32 = 3` is accepted because the initializer is a default unsuffixed integer literal that fits `u32`. `let size u32 = 3u64` and binding an existing `u64` to `u32` are type errors.
Write `let size u32 = u32(existing)` to request an explicit conversion. Conversion behavior, range checks, wrapping, and precision follow the named constructor's documented numeric family.

syntax.label: INITIALIZATION EXAMPLES
syntax.code:
let inferred = 3             # u64
let fitted u32 = 3           # u32
let explicit = u32(inferred) # u32
let label string = "ready"

sections.title: Expressions and Operators
sections.summary: Expressions include literals, names, lists, blocks, calls, member access, unary/binary operators, `try`/`catch`, `match`/`switch`, and postfix propagation.
paragraphs: Ordinary operands and call arguments evaluate from left to right. `if`, `and`, `or`, task forms, result combinators, and async wrappers are special forms because they control whether or where argument expressions evaluate.
Calls, member selection, and postfix `?` may chain. A block evaluates statements in lexical scope and returns its optional tail expression, or `null` when no tail is present.

syntax.label: EXPRESSION GRAMMAR

tables.title: Precedence from weakest to strongest
rows: The current parser consumes an operand at minimum tier 7. Consequently `-1 + 2` means `-(1 + 2)`; parenthesize unary operands in larger arithmetic.

sections.title: Functions, Closures, and Macros
sections.summary: A function is a runtime callable with immutable positional parameters, optional checked types, and lexical captures. A macro rewrites syntax before ordinary evaluation.
paragraphs: Write `func convert(value u32) string` for a typed declaration and `func(u32) string` for its callable type. An omitted annotation remains dynamic so existing source keeps its behavior.

Expression-bodied functions return the expression. Block-bodied functions return an explicit `return` value, their tail expression, or `null`. A bare `return` returns `null`. An annotated result checks every reachable return and fallthrough path.

Annotations never cast. Unsuffixed non-negative integer literals may inherit an expected numeric width, including the result alternatives of `if`, `match`/`switch`, `try`/`catch`, and block tails. Suffixed and existing values require an explicit constructor for conversion.
Nested functions may capture bindings from surrounding scopes. Backend support for closure conversion is feature-specific; unsupported native captures are compile-time diagnostics.

Macros use call syntax at their use site but substitute AST arguments into the declared expression body. Recursive expansion, wrong arity, invalid expansion, and type errors introduced by expansion are diagnosed before execution.

syntax.label: FUNCTION AND MACRO FORMS

sections.title: Statements and Control Flow
sections.summary: The statement grammar is deliberately small: declarations, output, loops, and explicit flow transfer.

tables.title: Statement forms
rows: Install an immutable lexical binding, optionally after fallibility propagation.
Install a mutable local cell or atomically replace it in source order. Only local `var` cells are assignable; aggregate values remain immutable.
Append one output value. Multiple expressions are rendered through `cat` with `", "` separators.
Repeat while the condition is truthy; observe cooperative cancellation at loop boundaries.
Iterate strings, lists, tensors, and other supported iterables in their defined order.
Leave the nearest function/block execution boundary with a value or `null`.
Leave or advance the nearest loop; use outside a loop is an error.
Introduce callable, syntactic, or nominal type names.

sections.title: Pattern Matching
sections.summary: `match` and `switch` evaluate their subject exactly once and select the first arm whose pattern and optional guard succeed.
paragraphs: A catch-all may be `_` or contextual `default`; `default` must be final and cannot have a guard. A guard follows contextual `when` and may use names bound by its pattern.
Closed enum matches are checked for duplicate, unreachable, invalid, and non-exhaustive arms. Alternative patterns must bind the same names.

syntax.label: MATCH GRAMMAR
syntax.code:
matchExpr   := ( "match" | "switch" ) expression "{" arm { ("," | ";") arm } "}"
arm         := ( pattern | "default" ) [ "when" expression ] "=>" expression
pattern     := conjunction { "|" conjunction }
conjunction := atom { "and" atom }
atom        := "_" | identifier | typeName identifier | literal
             | enumType "." caseName [ "(" [ pattern { "," pattern } ] ")" ]
             | ( "<" | "<=" | ">" | ">=" ) literal
             | "not" atom | "[" [ pattern { "," pattern } ] "]"
             | "(" pattern ")"

tables.title: Pattern categories
rows: Matches and binds the entire subject.
Matches exactly the listed length and recursively matches elements.
Matches nominal enum type, case, arity, and payload patterns.
Matches the named runtime kind and binds the value.
Compares the subject with a literal.
Combines, intersects, or negates pattern tests.

sections.title: Types, Runtime Kinds, and Truthiness
sections.summary: `Value` is the language boundary. Runtime values preserve kind, width/style, shape, ownership/resource state, nominal identity, and structured metadata where applicable.

tables.title: Numeric literal forms
rows: explicit floating style; unsuffixed fraction/exponent is `number`
pure imaginary `complex` retaining component style where supported

tables.title: Runtime kind strings
rows: zero; interval requires both endpoints zero
signed, unsigned, and packed integer families
nanosecond-precision instant with retained location identity
UTC, fixed-offset, or IANA timezone rules
ordered aggregate and shaped dense aggregate
failed, missing, or successful with a falsey payload
currently truthy only where the owning runtime path supplies an enum truthiness rule; use explicit matching for portable intent

paragraphs: Equality is structural for strings, lists, tensors, errors, results, options, enums, and compatible aggregates. Numeric equality performs the documented cross-family exact or floating conversion only where the runtime has a defined comparison.
Resources and callables do not have a general serialization or value-copy contract. `clone` and `view` make tensor ownership intent explicit.

sections.title: Packages, Modules, Imports, and Exports
sections.summary: File and standard-library modules expose ordered public member maps through an explicit alias.
paragraphs: `package name [version]` records module identity. `export a, b` defines the public names in stable source order. `import "reference" as alias` binds a module namespace.

A reference may include an exact, caret, or tilde semantic-version selector after `@`. Relative file imports are canonicalized beneath the project root, and generated lock/cache state is managed by `osiris mod`.

syntax.label: MODULE FORMS
syntax.code:
package geometry "1.2.0"
export area, perimeter
import "std/math@^1.0" as math
import "./shapes.osr" as shapes

tables.title: Standard modules
rows: Unicode-aware string comparison, search, cutting, splitting, trimming, replacement, and text shaping.
Numeric constructors, elementary/special functions, tensors, linear algebra, reductions, and `pi`/`tau`.
Stable hashing, mixing, deterministic noise, and seeded pseudo-random samples.
Context-aware TCP listen, accept, and dial.

Capability-gated command-line/environment access, bounded owned files and rooted filesystem operations, deterministic test providers, shell-free child processes, OS signal streams, and portable filesystem-watch events.
Exact durations, civil/Unix datetime construction, timezone conversion, parsing, formatting, arithmetic, components, comparison, and injected clock access.
Length, range, take, sum, and product.

sections.title: Errors, Result, Option, and Propagation
sections.summary: Recoverable failures use immutable structured errors and explicit `Result`/`Option` containers; fatal invariant failures use fatal structured errors.
paragraphs: `try expression catch name expression` catches recoverable failures. Postfix `?` and `let?` unwrap success/presence and propagate failure or absence. `unwrap`, `expect`, and the result combinators expose explicit functional alternatives.
An error record may carry kind/code, message, cause, source/location, stack, severity, public metadata, and separate debug metadata. `redact` removes stack/debug details before a trust boundary.

syntax.label: FALLIBILITY FORMS

sections.title: Tasks, Scheduling, Cancellation, and Async I/O
sections.summary: Concurrency is explicit through evaluator special forms. Cancellation is cooperative and context-based.

tables.title: Task special forms
rows: Starts one child evaluation and buffers its output.
Waits, merges ordered output, and propagates task failure/cancellation.
Requests cooperative cancellation; `true` only for a new request.
Computes concurrently, returns and commits output in source argument order.
Runs with a child deadline; commits output only on success.
Ordinary mode chooses first completion and cancels siblings.
Like `race`, with the source index. Task-debug mode deterministically chooses index 0.
Evaluates arguments first, then runs the blocking helper in a task.

sections.title: Execution and Backend Contract
sections.summary: The interpreter is the broad semantic implementation. VM and artifact backends support explicitly measured subsets recorded in the Backend Support matrix.
paragraphs: The bytecode VM must preserve interpreter-observable values, output order, errors, numeric style, and source behavior for supported programs.
The native path lowers Osiris IR to readable portable C and invokes a system C compiler. Unsupported lowering is a compile-time error; compilation never runs the program to manufacture output.
WASM and GPU commands emit artifacts for narrower documented subsets. A parser accepting syntax is not evidence that every execution backend supports it.

tables.title: Backend roles
rows: Tree-walking interpreter and broad runtime semantics.
IR-to-C inspection, object compilation, and native executable production.
GPU kernel source or versioned kernel-plan emission.

sections.title: Command-Line Reference
sections.summary: The CLI separates successful command payloads on standard output from diagnostics on standard error and uses stable categorized exit codes.

tables.title: Exit status
rows: Parse, type, analysis, or lowering failure.

syntax.label: MACHINE-READABLE FAILURES
syntax.code:
osiris --diagnostics=json <command> [arguments…]
# JSON schema v1 is written to stderr only when the command fails.

sections.title: Structs, Tuples, Aliases, and Newtypes
sections.summary: Product values are immutable, ordered, and explicit about nominal identity.

syntax.label: DECLARATIONS
VALUES
syntax.code:
Name { field: expression, … }
Name(argument, …)
value.field
value with { field: expression, … }
(expression, expression, …)
tuple[index]
let (name, name) = tuple

tables.title: Product-type rules
rows: Named or positional construction, field access, copied `with` update, structural equality
Indexing, destructuring, equality; heterogeneous item types are allowed
Explicit constructor naming an existing type; no new runtime kind
Explicit `Name(value)` construction and `.value` access; no implicit target conversion

tables.title: Field tags
rows: Backtick text contains space-separated `namespace:"value"` pairs; values use Go string escaping
The `json` namespace selects the serialized field name; `-` omits a field and `omitempty` omits empty values
Unknown tags are retained verbatim for codecs and tooling
Duplicate namespaces, malformed quoting, duplicate fields, and unknown initializer fields are source errors

paragraphs: Struct fields retain declaration order and declared type metadata. Struct values are immutable; `with` returns a copy with selected fields replaced. Tuples retain item order and support heterogeneous values.

Aliases are naming conveniences. Newtypes are nominal boundaries and require explicit construction or extraction. The interpreter and VM preserve these identities through equality, rendering, and codec round-trips; native C currently rejects product-type lowering at compile time rather than silently erasing identity.
